## The short version

*zotlook.org* is a set of static pages. There are **no cookies**, no tracking in
your browser, no user account and no sign-in. **Nothing is loaded from a
third-party server** — no fonts, maps, videos or scripts, and in particular no
Google Fonts. While you read these pages your browser talks to no server but
ours.

On the server itself the hosting provider produces **access statistics from
the truncated log files**. It needs no cookies and no scripts in your browser;
details below.

The only data processed is what arises technically when a page is requested.

## Requesting a page: server logs

On every request your browser transmits data that the web server records in a
log file:

- a **truncated** IP address of your device, see below
- the date and time of the request
- the address requested and the amount of data transferred
- the HTTP status code
- the referring page, if your browser sends one
- browser and operating system (user agent)

**Your IP address is not stored in full.** The web server truncates it before
writing anything: for IPv4 it replaces the last byte with a random value, for
IPv6 it anonymises the last 88 bits. The logs therefore cannot identify your
connection.

**Purpose:** operating the site — delivering pages, detecting and repelling
attacks, and finding faults.

**Legal basis:** Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is the secure
and uninterrupted operation of the website.

**Retention:** logs are deleted automatically after seven days. Individual
entries are kept longer only where a specific security incident requires it,
and then only until it has been resolved.

The logs are not analysed to trace the behaviour of individual people, and
they are not combined with other data.

## Hosting

The pages are served from a machine operated by

**Hetzner Online GmbH**, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany

in a data centre in Germany. Hetzner processes the data listed above solely on
our behalf and on our instructions, under a data processing agreement pursuant
to Article 28 GDPR. The data does not leave the European Union.

## Access statistics: AWStats and Report Magic

The hosting provider's console analyses the log files described above with
**AWStats** and **Report Magic** and produces access statistics from them —
page requests, volumes transferred, browsers, referring pages. This is stated
explicitly because both are a fixed part of the hosting package and **cannot
be switched off**.

Five points make the difference from ordinary web analytics:

* The analysis happens **on the server**, not in your browser. Nothing is
  stored on your device and nothing is read from it — no cookies, no scripts,
  no tracking pixels. Consent under § 25 TDDG is therefore not required, which
  is why you see no consent dialogue here.
* It works **only on the already truncated logs**. Truncation happens on the
  web server before anything is written, so the statistics never see your full
  IP address at any point.
* **No third party is involved.** The analysis runs on the same machine in
  Germany and the results do not leave it.
* We can view the statistics in the hosting console. They show totals and
  distributions, not the recognition of individual people.
* The reports remain available after the underlying logs have been deleted
  seven days on. What remains is aggregate figures only.

**Legal basis:** Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, to the extent the truncated data is
personal data at all. The legitimate interest is being able to judge how the
site is running.

## Search on these pages

Search runs entirely in your browser. A search index is downloaded once as a
file; from then on searching happens locally on your device. Your search terms
are **not** transmitted to the server and are not stored anywhere.

## Contacting us by email

If you write to us, we process your address and the content of your message in
order to answer it. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, or Article 6(1)(b)
where the enquiry concerns a contract. We keep the correspondence for as long
as follow-up questions are to be expected and delete it afterwards, unless a
statutory retention period applies.

## Links to other websites

These pages link to third-party sites, in particular to DOI addresses of
academic literature, to source code repositories and to the sites of other
software. Those links become active **only when you click them**. Until then
the provider concerned learns nothing about your visit. After that its own
privacy policy applies, over which we have no influence.

## What the plugin itself sends

zotLook runs on your own machine and sends no usage data, no error reports
and nothing about your library or your documents to us or to anyone else.
Your attachments and annotations stay where Zotero keeps them.

**It asks for updates.** Like every Zotero plugin, zotLook checks once a day
whether a newer version exists. Copies installed from version 1.6.0 onwards
ask `zotlook.org/update.json`; that request reaches our web server and is
logged as described above, with the address truncated before it is written.
We count the number of such requests per day, which tells us roughly how many
copies are in use, and nothing else; the count cannot be traced to anyone.
Earlier copies ask GitHub for the same file instead. The update itself, when
there is one, is downloaded from GitHub, where
[GitHub's privacy statement](https://docs.github.com/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement)
applies. Zotero's own settings decide whether plugins are updated
automatically.

If you run Zotero with Zotero's sync service, that is your decision and your
own contractual relationship; we are not party to it.

## Your rights

You have the right to access (Article 15 GDPR), rectification (Article 16),
erasure (Article 17), restriction of processing (Article 18) and data
portability (Article 20).

**Right to object:** where we process data on the basis of a legitimate
interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR), you may object under Article 21 GDPR on
grounds relating to your particular situation.

We do not ask for consent, because we do not need any. There is accordingly
nothing to withdraw.

## No automated decision-making

There is no automated decision-making, including profiling, within the meaning
of Article 22 GDPR.
